close_reason: Done in commit. from_der_iter rustdoc now explicitly says fail-fast and notes the iterator is not drained after the first failure.
description:
pkix-truststore/src/lib.rs:362 documents from_der_iter as:

  /// The iterator is consumed eagerly; all anchors are decoded before returning.

Read literally, this implies collect-all-then-report semantics: every iterator
item is polled, every blob is attempted, then a single error (perhaps with
multiple problems aggregated) is returned. That is what 'all anchors are
decoded' says in English.

The impl at lib.rs:377-380 is fail-fast:

  for (i, bytes) in iter.into_iter().enumerate() {
      let cert = Certificate::from_der(bytes.as_ref()).map_err(|_| Error::MalformedAnchor(i))?;
      anchors.push(TrustAnchor::from_cert(cert));
  }

The `?` exits at the first malformed entry. The iterator is dropped without
polling subsequent items. The Error::MalformedAnchor doc text on lib.rs:233-236
is consistent with fail-fast (it refers to 'the offending entry,' singular).
The function-level doc on lib.rs:362 is not.

What goes wrong for a caller in production:

  - A caller relying on the docs to write 'I expect this to either succeed or
    surface the first failure index' is correct in practice, wrong in docs.
  - A caller relying on the docs to write 'I can pass an infinite or expensive
    iterator and trust that all items will be polled before return' is wrong:
    fail-fast means an iterator that produces items lazily from a network or
    HSM stops being polled after the first bad item. That may be the desired
    behavior, but the caller cannot know it from the docs.
  - A caller writing a wrapping adapter that needs to know whether the
    iterator is fully drained after a Result::Err return (for cleanup,
    resource release, or retry) cannot tell from the docs.

Fix: rewrite the line to state fail-fast plainly. Suggested:

  /// The iterator is consumed eagerly (not lazy). On the first malformed
  /// entry, the function returns Err(Error::MalformedAnchor(i)) where i is
  /// the 0-based index of the failing item, and the rest of the iterator
  /// is not polled.

This pairs naturally with PKIX-tit4.3 (which surfaces the missing der::Error
in MalformedAnchor) — fixing both gives callers a precise contract for the
adapter entry point.
title: Doc/impl mismatch: from_der_iter claims 'all anchors are decoded before returning' but impl is fail-fast
